extracted.intended_audience: Exchange administrators, State insurance regulators, agents/brokers/web-brokers, and stakeholders submitting comments on ACA Exchange rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedures for verifying income eligibility for Advance Premium Tax Credit (APTC) and Cost Sharing Reductions (CSRs), and for enforcing Exchange agreements (including termination for cause) for agents, brokers, and web-brokers on Federally-facilitated Exchanges and State-based Exchanges on the Federal platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preponderance of the evidence standard for termination
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS would apply a “preponderance of the evidence” standard of proof with respect to issues of fact to assess potential noncompliance under §155.220(g)(1) and make a determination there was a specific finding or pattern of noncompliance that is sufficiently severe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed definition at §155.20: “preponderance of the evidence” means proof by evidence that, compared with evidence opposing it, leads to the conclusion that the fact at issue is more likely true than not. Rationale compares this standard to clear-and-convincing, substantial evidence, and beyond-a-reasonable-doubt standards and notes that preponderance is commonly used in Federal civil and administrative proceedings. HHS seeks comment on whether a different standard would be more appropriate given potential consequences (including effects on State licensure and loss of ability to assist with Exchange enrollments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination-for-cause applicability to agents, brokers, web-brokers
rubrics_metrics.description: Termination for cause standards in §155.220(l) and §155.220(g)(1)-(3) apply to agents, brokers, and web-brokers participating in SBE-FPs and FFEs for noncompliance with applicable law, regulatory requirements, and Exchange agreement terms and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences described include termination of Exchange agreements, notification to State insurance oversight agencies (potentially affecting State licensure), and loss of ability to assist with enrollment or applications for APTC and CSRs for QHPs offered through Exchanges. HHS seeks input on actions or subject matters to be specifically outlined in Exchange agreements for PY 2026+.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange agreements must specify impermissible conduct and consent documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed increased specificity in Exchange agreements for PY 2026 and beyond regarding impermissible conduct by agents, brokers, and web-brokers and requirements to ensure agents/brokers/web-brokers have obtained and documented consumer consent to collect PII and help apply/enroll in QHP coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes intended to provide clear guidance on conduct and on how HHS will address compliance failures; HHS requests comments on what actions/subjects should be specifically outlined or emphasized in future Exchange agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant obligation to provide most recent tax return information
rubrics_metrics.description: For applicants claiming PTC or CSR, the ACA requires them to provide income information from their most recent tax return filing; if there are changes in circumstances or when the tax filer was not required to file taxes, applicants must report additional income information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement derives from section 1411(b)(3)(A) and (C) of the ACA; the rulemaking emphasizes the importance of filing Federal income tax returns when required because APTC is set based on recent tax-year income.

rubrics_metrics.name: APTC must be set based on most recent taxable year's household income
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1412(b)(1)(B) requires APTC to be set on the basis of the individual's household income for the most recent taxable year for which information is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS emphasizes the imperative that consumers file required Federal income tax returns because the tax return is a primary basis for accurate income estimates used to set APTC; failing to file can lead to inaccurate APTC amounts and potential tax liabilities that the Federal Government cannot fully recover for many households.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS responsibility for verification and use of trusted data sources
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS is responsible for verifying and determining income eligibility, including verifying household income with the IRS and other trusted third-party data sources (e.g., SSA, DHS), and establishing a robust data matching program and compatible electronic information exchange systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory basis: sections 1411, 1413, and 1414 of the ACA. The interface must be compatible with methods for data verification under section 1411(c)(4). HHS may delegate verification responsibilities to Exchanges when IRS cannot verify income, but HHS retains authority to regulate and guide how Exchanges perform verification and to oversee the data matching program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchanges' intermediary role and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges operate as the intermediary between applicants and HHS: they must submit applicant information to HHS, provide notice to applicants, collect documentary evidence, and facilitate efforts to resolve income inconsistencies with the IRS or HHS verification sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If HHS delegates verification to Exchanges under section 1411(d), Exchanges still must follow HHS guidance. Exchanges make the final connection with applicants to resolve outstanding income inconsistencies and are responsible for collecting evidence and facilitating resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data matching inconsistency (DMI) resolution process and 90-day period
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant-provided household income is inconsistent with IRS tax filing information or fails verification under section 1411(d), Exchanges must make reasonable efforts to identify and address causes (including clerical errors), contact the applicant to confirm accuracy, and take additional actions as HHS may identify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inconsistency persists, the Exchange must notify the applicant and give them 90 calendar days from the notice date to either present satisfactory documentary evidence to the Exchange or resolve the inconsistency with the IRS or HHS verification source. If unresolved at end of 90 days, section 1411(e)(4)(B)(ii) requires the Exchange to set APTC and CSR based on IRS income information and information provided to HHS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission requirement for verifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 1411(c)(4)(A), HHS must conduct income verifications and determinations through electronic submission of applicant information and responses, except HHS may use a different method for income inconsistencies than the IRS per section 1411(c)(4)(B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ACA directs HHS to establish compatible electronic interfaces for Exchanges and State agencies to participate in secure data matching and to streamline eligibility determinations across Federal and State subsidy programs (section 1413).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure To File Taxes and Reconcile (FTR) eligibility limitation (§155.305(f)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendment to §155.305(f)(4): an Exchange may not determine a tax filer or their enrollee eligible for APTC if (1) HHS notifies the Exchange that APTC were paid on behalf of the tax filer (or spouse) for a year used for verification, and (2) the tax filer did not comply with the requirement to file a Federal income tax return and reconcile APTC for that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proposal would reinstate the previous FTR policy (pre-COVID PHE) intended to prevent accumulation of tax liabilities and improper enrollments. HHS discusses operational history (FTR Recheck, direct vs indirect notices, pause during COVID-19 PHE) and requests comment on impacts. The proposal is aimed at program integrity, though HHS acknowledges potential consumer continuity tradeoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: FTR timing policy: one-tax-year vs two-tax-year framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy choice whether to deny APTC eligibility after one tax year of non-filing/reconciling (one-tax-year FTR) versus after two consecutive tax years of non-filing/reconciling (two-tax-year FTR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS previously changed to a two-tax-year rule to mitigate operational issues and continuity of coverage; later required FTR warning notices for one-year nonfilers. HHS now proposes reverting to the pre-PHE one-tax-year policy to reduce risk of accumulated tax liabilities and to act as a backstop against improper enrollments (evidence cited of lead-generation schemes and improper enrollments). HHS solicits comment on tradeoffs including tax liability risk and improper enrollment mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: FTR notice requirements and FTI safeguards (direct vs indirect notices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges may send direct notices to tax filers, indirect notices to enrollees, or both. Direct notices that explicitly inform tax filers they will lose APTC for failure to file/reconcile require FTI-compliant infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically, an FTR direct-notice carve-out required Exchanges to send direct notification before denying APTC; operational limitations led to temporary changes. The availability of direct notices affects ability to run recheck processes and how soon enrollees receive urgency messaging about filing/reconciling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that applicants file Federal income taxes and reconcile when receiving APTC/CSR
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants bear responsibility to file Federal income taxes for any year that they receive APTC and CSR, and, if circumstances change or they were not required to file, to report and attest to accurate income information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This responsibility is central to the verification framework; failure to file/reconcile leads to FTR consequences (possible loss of APTC) and may create substantial tax liabilities. HHS notes administrative burdens of filing but underscores statutory expectation under sections 6011/6012 of the Code and ACA verification provisions.
